units.source_text: 以后，每当见到夫人，我都很担心，

en.t: After that, whenever I saw his wife, I felt uneasy,

units.source_text: 先生对夫人难道也一直是这样的态度吗？

en.t: Could Sensei really always behave this way toward his wife as well?

units.source_text: 果真如此的话，夫人会满意吗？

en.t: If that was truly so, would his wife be content with it?

units.source_text: 夫人的神情叫人猜不透她是否满意，

en.t: His wife's expression made it impossible to tell whether she was satisfied or not,

units.source_text: 因为我也没有更多的机会接近夫人，

en.t: because I had no greater opportunity to become close to her,

units.source_text: 而且她每次见到我，又总是表现得一如平常。

en.t: and every time she saw me, she always behaved just as usual.

units.source_text: 况且，先生若是不在家，我和夫人也很少见面。

en.t: Besides, when Sensei was not at home, his wife and I rarely met.

units.source_text: 更加令我不解的是，先生对于人性的这种看法是怎么产生的。

en.t: What puzzled me even more was how Sensei had come to hold this view of human nature.

units.source_text: 难道这只是他以冷酷的目光内省自己、观察社会的结果吗？

en.t: Was it merely the result of coldly examining himself and observing society?

units.source_text: 先生善于坐着思考，那么，

en.t: Sensei was good at sitting still and thinking, so then,

units.source_text: 只要有先生那样的头脑，坐在家里思考人生，就会自然而然地产生这种看法吗？

en.t: if one had a mind like his, would sitting at home and thinking about life naturally produce such a view?

units.source_text: 先生的看法似乎是鲜活的，
它不同于被火烧过的冰凉石头房屋的空架子。

en.t: unlike the empty shell of a cold stone house that had been burned by fire.

units.source_text: 在我眼里，先生的确是一位思想家。

en.t: In my eyes, Sensei was indeed a thinker.

units.source_text: 但是，在这位思想家归纳出来的主义里，

en.t: But within the principles this thinker had formulated,

units.source_text: 似乎编织进了沉痛的事实，

en.t: there seemed to be painful facts woven in,

units.source_text: 这些事实不是同自己无关的别人的事，

en.t: facts that were not someone else's affairs, unrelated to him,

units.source_text: 而是蕴含着某种令人痛彻肺腑、热血沸腾、脉搏停跳的真实。

en.t: but truths of a kind that could pierce the heart, make the blood run hot, and stop the pulse.
